trend.summary: In 2024, IonQ is focused on developing quantum computers aimed at solving complex global problems and transforming various sectors. The company is actively expanding its technical capabilities, including reallocating engineering resources and integrating new technologies, while supporting multi-year simulation roadmaps in related industries like solid-state battery chemistry.
IonQ believes that offering QCaaS can accelerate adoption of its quantum computing solutions while efficiently promoting quantum computing across its partner ecosystems.

ps_5e9b07c018.text: This process allows the creation of quantum logic gates between any pair of qubits, regardless of their distance within the crystal, which can be arbitrarily reconfigured in software.

ps_38f19bd17b.text: Many other quantum systems rely upon fabricated qubits, which bring about imprecisions such that no single qubit is exactly the same as any other qubit in the system.

ps_a3d67e0f12.text: This memo consolidates findings from the Q2 technical review cycle and addresses three intersecting priorities: (1) the accuracy of quantum networking performance claims in external-facing materials, (2) near-term engineering capacity reallocation tied to legacy system wind-down, and (3) status updates on the Q-CTRL integration test and the Customer Success quarterly review cycle.
ps_a3d67e0f12.claim: IonQ's July 11, 2024 memo consolidates Q2 technical review findings and covers quantum networking claim accuracy, engineering capacity reallocation tied to legacy system wind-down, and status of the Q-CTRL integration test.

ps_a277d600c7.text: The point at which a quantum computer is able to perform a particular computation that exceeds its classical counterpart in speed or reduces its cost to solution is known as the point of “quantum advantage.”

ps_03d387bf79.text: We provide QCaaS, complemented by access to quantum experts and algorithm development capabilities.

ps_cdd4becd14.text: As part of this roadmap, we introduced the notion of “algorithmic qubits” as a metric to measure progress, and a detailed description of how to define and measure the number of algorithmic qubits (#AQ) in early 2022.
